description: Silicon is a hard, brittle crystalline solid with a blue-grey metallic lustre. It is a tetravalent non-metal sometimes considered a metalloid and semiconductor, belonging to group 14 of the periodic table. It is relatively unreactive and the eighth most common element in the universe by mass, though it rarely occurs in pure form in the Earth's crust.
uses: Silicon is widely used as a semiconductor material in transistors, solar cells, and integrated circuits. It is used commercially in industrial construction with clays, silica sand, and stone, as well as in Portland cement, concrete, ceramics, and glass. Silicon compounds like silicon carbide are used as abrasives and in high-strength ceramics, and silicon is the basis of silicone polymers.
characteristics: Silicon has a melting point of 1414 °C and boiling point of 3265 °C, which are the second highest among all metalloids and nonmetals. As a semiconductor, its resistivity decreases as temperature rises due to a small energy gap between its valence and conduction bands. Pure silicon is effectively an insulator at room temperature but becomes conductive when doped with elements such as phosphorus or boron.
